title: TEMPLATE SAMPLE — Buyer's Playbook format (content from 001, not for publishing)

lines.say: Four thousand pieces. In stock. Ships today.

lines: Real stock, or bait? Five checks before you pay a broker.

lines.text: I'm Leo. I trade components in Shenzhen.
lines.say: I'm Leo. I trade components in Shenzhen.

visual.label: DDR5 server memory fulfillment for traditional OEMs
visual.note: REPORTEDLY · SUPPLY GOES TO HYPERSCALERS FIRST

lines.text: Memory is on allocation. Traditional OEMs reportedly get under 30% of their DDR5 orders.
lines.say: Memory is on allocation. Traditional O-E-Ms reportedly get under thirty percent of their D-D-R five orders.

lines: One. Ask for a photo taken today, with the date and your company name.
Bait stock usually stops right here.

visual.caption: D/C · EXAMPLE YYWW · NO D/C FIELD? CHECK LOT

lines: Two. Check the date code. Reels should match, and the date should make sense.
Impossible date codes often mean re-marked parts.

title: LABEL
= MAKER.
visual.note: EXAMPLE · LABEL FORMATS VARY BY MAKER

lines: Three. Part number, quantity and lot should match what the maker issued.
Not sure? Ask the manufacturer or an authorized distributor.
Four. Ask for the certificate of conformance, and where the parts came from.
No paper trail is a red flag.

title: THIRD-PARTY
TEST.
visual.tag: REAL STOCK? THE ANSWER IS YES.

lines: Five. Ask if they'll accept third-party testing, like X-ray at an independent lab.
A seller with real stock says yes.
Five checks. Save this for your next urgent order.
Buyer's Playbook. Every Friday. Sources in the caption.
